analysis:
All three changed files are test-only (provider-swift/Tests/...). No production source, protocol, key custody, attestation, or encryption code is modified in the supplied evidence.

1) ModelPrefixBenchmarkFixture.swift (head lines 46-51): checkpointEnvironment now also sets the prefill-chunk and step-token-budget environment variables from CBv2SchedulerConfig() defaults whenever a solo-prefill stripe is pinned. This only affects the qualification fixture's scheduler geometry. The cache-root test env vars (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_TEST_ROOT, ALLOW_EPHEMERAL) are unchanged, as are the persistent-namespace validation and the cleanup behavior (root removal only for the non-persistent case). I saw no change to the T-041 at-rest posture: HMAC names, TTL, DBK3 crypto and KEK custody are untouched.

2) ModelCheckpointStorageSpecificationTests.swift (head lines 75-76): adds assertions for the new env keys. It also pins the exact key set of the fixture environment (lines 66-67), which guards against ambient precision overrides leaking in.

3) LaunchAgentRestartTests.swift (head lines 182-204): new test forwardsPrefillGeometryRollbackToProviderJob asserts that prefillChunkKey and stepTokenBudgetKey pass through LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvironment, that UNRELATED_SECRET is excluded, and that WatchdogAgent does not forward them. It exercises the allowlist (a negative secret-exclusion check) but changes no allowlist itself in this diff. The production allowlist change that this test presumes (inferencePassthroughEnvKeys containing the two keys) is not in the supplied batch. If a companion production change exists elsewhere in the PR, it should be reviewed for the launchd environment surface. These are non-secret numeric tuning values whose malformed input handling lives in EngineV2Factory.prefillGeometry, which was not supplied, so I make no claim about it.

No security regression is identified in the supplied test code. Remaining integration question: confirm that the production allowlist and EngineV2Factory.prefillGeometry validate and bound these values, since a wide chunk could affect memory/availability (T-010/T-029 class) but this is not demonstrable from the test-only evidence.
